subject: Cloud Computing
title: Redundancy and Backup Power
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Redundancy and Backup Power.

hook.text: When the power goes out at your house, your lights turn off. At a data center, nothing can stop.

buildup.text: Data centers use UPS batteries that kick in within milliseconds of a power failure.

discovery.text: Diesel generators start within seconds, providing power for days if the grid stays down.

twist.text: Everything is duplicated: power feeds, cooling systems, network connections. Failure of one changes nothing.

climax.text: Top-tier data centers guarantee 99.999% uptime — that's about five minutes of downtime per year.

punchline.text: The cloud stays on because everything exists twice. At least.

quiz.question: How do data centers handle power outages?
options: UPS batteries bridge the gap until diesel generators take over
They immediately shut down and restart when power returns
Solar panels on the roof provide emergency backup power

details.summary: Cloud data centers maintain multiple layers of power redundancy including utility feeds from separate substations, battery backup systems that last minutes, and diesel generators that can run for days. No single power failure can take down a properly designed cloud facility.
details.whyItMatters: Power redundancy is the foundation of cloud reliability. Understanding how providers protect against power failures explains the high availability guarantees in cloud SLAs.
takeaways: Multiple utility power feeds provide the first layer of redundancy
UPS batteries bridge the gap during power transitions
Diesel generators can sustain operations for days

faq.question: What happens when the power goes out at a data center?
faq.answer: UPS battery systems instantly take over, providing power within milliseconds. Diesel generators start within seconds and fully take over within a minute. The batteries bridge this gap seamlessly so servers never lose power. Most facilities can run on generators indefinitely.

faq.question: How many layers of power redundancy exist?
faq.answer: Tier 4 data centers use N+1 or 2N redundancy, meaning they have double the power capacity needed. Multiple utility feeds, battery banks, and generator sets ensure that even multiple simultaneous failures cannot cause a power outage. Critical systems have three or more independent power paths.
